title: Multicenter characterization of enterocolitis associated with BCMA-directed CAR T cell therapy
desc: Immune effector cell-associated enterocolitis (IEC-EC) is a delayed toxicity of ciltacabtagene autoleucel. The US Multiple Myeloma Immunotherapy Consortium retrospectively adjudicated 54 suspected cases from 8 institutions: 41 were IEC-EC (31 confirmed by anti-camelid variable heavy-chain immunohistochemistry, 10 probable). Through September 2025, cumulative incidence was 3.0% (39 of 1,308 ciltacabtagene autoleucel recipients; 95% CI 2.1–4.1%); 12-month competing-risk incidence was 3.0% (95% CI 2.1–4.1%). Median symptom onset was 75 days after infusion. Grade ≥3 diarrhea occurred in 85% (34 of 40 with diarrhea); 73% (30 of 41) required parenteral nutrition. Despite normal upper endoscopy in 41% (9 of 22), duodenal biopsies showed villous blunting, apoptotic bodies and a dense cytotoxic T cell infiltrate, CD4+ in 61% (19 of 31), CD8+ in 26% (8 of 31) and mixed in 13% (4 of 31). A dominant T cell clone was detected in 76% (13 of 17 tested). Delayed neurotoxicity co-occurred in 41% (17 of 41). At last follow-up, 32% (13 of 41) resolved, 27% (11 of 41) had ongoing symptoms and 41% (17 of 41) died with active IEC-EC. Combined biologic and T cell-directed therapy yielded the highest resolution (55%, 6 of 11) in small subgroups. IEC-EC is potentially fatal and requires systematic evaluation and early directed therapy.

title: Metastatic Prostate Cancer Treatment Variation in Veterans.
desc: [JAMA network open] Not all men with metastatic castration-sensitive prostate cancer (mCSPC) receive the recommended combination therapy of androgen deprivation therapy (ADT) plus an androgen receptor pathway inhibitor (ARPI) and/or chemotherapy. To determine factors associated with combination therapy use among veterans with mCSPC in the national Veterans Health Administration (VHA) system. This cohort study included US veterans diagnosed with mCSPC between January 1, 2023, through December 31, 2024, who were followed up through June 30, 2025. National multicenter data were obtained from the VHA electronic health record, community care settings (private care paid with VHA benefits), and Medicare. All included veterans were identified through a validated natural language processing algorithm, were followed up in the VHA for at least 2 years prior to their metastatic diagnosis, were provided ADT within the first 6 months of diagnosis, and received no prostate cancer-directed therapy in the year prior to diagnosis. Clinical factors (eg, comorbidities, frailty, prostate cancer burden at diagnosis) and nonclinical factors (eg, annual household income, neighborhood disadvantage) were investigated to determine their association with the outcome. The primary outcome was receipt of combination therapy (ie, ADT plus ARPI [abiraterone, enzalutamide, apalutamide, darolutamide] and/or docetaxel) vs ADT alone. Information on these treatments was obtained through pharmacy records. Multilevel logistic regression models were used and marginal predicted probabilities were reported to determine the associations of factors with receipt of combination therapy. Variation among VHA facilities was reported. A total of 4023 veterans (mean [SD] age, 75.3 [8.0] years) met eligibility criteria. Of these patients, 2339 (58.1%) had de novo metastatic disease, while 1684 (41.9%) had recurrent disease. Overall, 2564 patients (63.7%) received combination therapy. In adjusted analyses, older veterans (eg, aged 85-89 years: predicted probability, -14.1 [95% CI, -20.5 to -8.2] percentage points [pp]) and veterans with more comorbidities (eg, congestive heart failure: predicted probability, -7.5 [95% CI, -12.9 to -2.5] pp) were less likely to receive combination therapy. Annual household income and neighborhood disadvantage were not associated with receipt of combination therapy. title: Multicenter evaluation of radiomics and multimodal artificial intelligence for colorectal cancer diagnosis and survival prediction
desc: Reliable preoperative classification and outcome prediction could improve management of locally advanced colorectal cancer. We retrospectively studied 879 participants from two centers, including 741 patients with locally advanced colorectal cancer and 138 with benign colorectal lesions. Clinical, radiomics, deep learning, and early fusion models were trained at center A (n = 615) and independently tested at center B (n = 264) using pretreatment contrast-enhanced computed tomography and clinical data. The clinical-radiomics nomogram achieved a test AUC of 0.957 for benign-malignant classification. For 3-year and 5-year overall survival, radiomics achieved test AUCs of 0.874 and 0.898, while fusion achieved 0.870 and 0.899, respectively. These findings identify CT radiomics as a promising digital biomarker for colorectal cancer stratification and show that early deep learning fusion offers limited incremental value over an optimized radiomics baseline.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Lung Diseases: Screening, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prognosis.
source: PubMed · Methods in molecular biology (Clifton, N.J.)
desc: [Methods in molecular biology (Clifton, N.J.)] Pulmonary diseases currently pose significant threats to global health, spanning common chronic conditions including lung cancer, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), and asthma, as well as infectious and inflammatory diseases like tuberculosis, interstitial lung disease (ILD), and COVID-19. Therefore, accurate diagnosis, effective therapeutic strategies, and reliable assessment of prognosis for pulmonary diseases are essential for improving patient outcomes and safeguarding public health. Despite the increasing availability of medical imaging and pathological data owing to improvements in detection technologies, what is becoming increasingly evident are the limitations of conventional diagnosis, which relies solely on clinicians' subjective judgment based on imaging, pulmonary function, pathology, and clinical experience. In recent years, artificial intelligence (AI) technology, especially machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL), has made significant progress in areas such as image recognition and model construction. Numerous studies have demonstrated the widespread application of AI in the screening and diagnosis of lung diseases, the optimization of treatment strategies, and prognosis assessment, revealing its remarkable ability to process and interpret complex clinical data. Although concerns persist regarding data quality, the "black box" nature of algorithms, clinical practice, and the regulatory landscape, the application of AI in lung disease research and clinical care is more and more promising. In this review, we summarize the latest advances of AI in the diagnosis and treatment of pulmonary diseases, analyze the challenges and limitations of current AI technologies ranging from data and algorithms to clinical translation, and highlight directions for future research.

title: AI-Based Anatomy Recognition in Minimally Invasive Kidney Surgery
desc: [Newly registered clinical trial, no results yet; sponsor: Chinese PLA General Hospital; conditions: Kidney (Renal Cell) Cancer, Ureteropelvic Junction Obstruction, Upper Urinary Tract Carcinoma; type: OBSERVATIONAL; enrollment: 1700; status: NOT_YET_RECRUITING] This study aims to evaluate whether an artificial intelligence (AI) based software system can assist surgeons in identifying key anatomical structures during minimally invasive upper urinary tract surgery. During these procedures, surgeons operate while viewing images from laparoscopic endoscope. Key anatomical structures, such as the kidney, renal artery and vein, ureter, renal pelvis, inferior vena cava, and left reproductive vein, as well as surgical targets such as tumors, may sometimes be difficult to distinguish because of bleeding, surgical smoke, tissue movement, changes in tissue appearance, or obstruction by surgical instruments. The study team has developed an AI-based image recognition system that analyzes surgical video in real time and identifies and outlines relevant anatomical structures on the screen during surgery. The study has two main goals (primary endpoints): 1. To evaluate how accurately the AI system can identify and delineate key anatomical structures in surgical videos collected from different hospitals, surgeons, surgical procedures, and imaging systems. 2. To evaluate the real-time performance and technical reliability of the AI system in the operating room, including processing latency, frame rate, system failure rate, and the proportion of time during surgery in which AI-generated results are successfully displayed. The study will include adults aged 18 years or older who undergo one of five types of minimally invasive upper urinary tract surgery: partial nephrectomy, radical nephrectomy, radical nephroureterectomy, inferior vena cava tumor thrombectomy, or pyeloplasty. The study will be conducted at 11 hospitals in China. In the first phase, surgical videos recorded between 2015 and 2025 will be used to develop, validate, and test the AI system. In the second phase, approximately 100 patients will be prospectively enrolled from internal centers, and the AI-generated anatomical recognition results will be displayed on a monitor during surgery. Overall, approximately 1,600 retrospective surgical cases and 100 prospective cases are planned for inclusion. The AI system is designed solely as an assistive tool for anatomical recognition. It does not make clinical decisions, provide autonomous surgical instructions, or control any surgical equipment. Surgeons remain fully responsible for all clinical and surgical decisions, and the AI display can be turned off at any time. All participants will receive standard clinical care. Parti

title: Flexible Multi-Stack Super-Resolution of Clinical Brain MRI Using Hetero-Orientation Variational Encoding: Expert Reader Evaluation in a Nigerian Cohort
desc: High-resolution brain MRI is important for neuroradiological assessment, yet routine clinical protocols often rely on fast, anisotropic 2D acquisitions, particularly in resource-constrained settings. These acquisitions may differ in orientation, alignment and anatomical coverage, resulting in partially overlapping image stacks. Existing learning-based super-resolution methods typically rely on single, under-constrained inputs or fixed multi-stack configurations with idealised acquisition geometry. We introduce MS-HVED, a sequence-agnostic framework for flexible multi-stack brain MRI super-resolution. Available axial, coronal and sagittal stacks are independently encoded into multi-scale Gaussian posteriors and fused using a field-of-view-aware Product-of-Gaussians formulation that limits contributions from unsupported regions. Physics-informed domain randomisation simulates heterogeneous clinical acquisition conditions, including obliqueness, partial coverage and imaging artefacts. MS-HVED achieved competitive or superior reconstruction fidelity across synthetic benchmarks and improved downstream tissue segmentation relative to low-resolution inputs. To assess generalisation beyond the training cohorts, we performed external clinical validation on 30 routine brain MRI examinations from a Nigerian cohort, representing an under-represented population in medical imaging research. These examinations formed the largest component of a blinded reader study involving 44 real cases and seven expert neuroradiologists. In the Nigerian cohort, MS-HVED was preferred over the supervised baseline for overall image quality in 187 of 210 paired assessments. Across all clinical cohorts, MS-HVED achieved higher overall-quality scores with all available inputs (5.93 vs. 4.49, p<.001), with the preference persisting when axial or coronal inputs were omitted (p<.001). title: A Neurosymbolic Multimodal Framework for 30-Day Diabetic Readmission Prediction: Integrating Structured EHR Data, Dense Clinical Embeddings, and Knowledge-Grounded Symbolic Extraction
desc: Unplanned 30-day readmissions among patients with diabetes mellitus impose a substantial clinical and economic burden, yet most predictive models use only structured electronic health record (EHR) data and ignore free-text clinical notes, which often contain code-mixed Hindi-English (Hinglish) phrasing and negation that general-purpose language models parse unreliably. We propose a neurosymbolic multimodal framework evaluated on the public Diabetes 130-US Hospitals dataset (101,766 encounters; 71,518 patients) with a patient-level grouped 80/20 split. title: Eye-to-Eye: Gaze detection as a proxy for medical doctor behaviour during virtual and in-person appointments
desc: The gaze direction of the physician during consultations plays an important role in patient satisfaction, with several studies pointing to the positive correlation between the amount of time the physician spends looking at the patient and patient satisfaction. Additionally, the effects of the virtual consultation environment on the gaze behaviour of the doctor have yet to be studied. Therefore, this study aims to assess the impact of the virtual consultation environment by comparing the amount of total time the doctor spends looking at the patient between face-to-face and virtual consultations, as well as the average duration during the consultation and the gaze frequency. The study population consisted of 14 doctors divided between 4 medical specialties: Gynaecology/Obstetrics (4), Neurology (3), Endocrinology (3) and General and Familiar Medicine (4). A low-cost desktop that runs an appearance-based gaze estimation pipeline was implemented in the clinical setup. Each doctor recorded 20 face-to-face consultations and 20 virtual consultations, which were then processed by the pipeline to obtain the percentage of time the doctor spent looking at the patient during the consultation. Overall, we found that doctors look more at the patient in virtual consultations compared to face-to-face consultations, both in total time and average duration during the consultation. Within medical specialties, three out the four specialties involved presented clear tendencies to look more at the patient in virtual consultations when compared to face-to-face consultations.

title: GenVinci reconstructs 3D molecular tissue scenes from histology to map senescence across aging and disease
desc: Spatial omics has generated measurements at unprecedented scale, yet computational approaches remain largely confined to individual modalities and 2D representations. Here we assemble ImageOmicsNet-300M, a corpus of 300 million single-cell and spatial transcriptomic profiles, including 24.9 million H&E-predicted virtual spatial transcriptomics profiles, and 4,623 H&E sections. Of these H&E sections, we generated 1,782 from aging mouse organs and serially sectioned human skin spanning five decades, with matched spatial transcriptomics and snRNA-seq. Building on this resource, we develop GenVinci, a multimodal tissue foundation model that reconstructs 3D tissue scenes from routine 2D histology. GenVinci predicts spatial gene expression from H&E with zero-shot generalization and maps senescence-associated states across 85.8 million cells, revealing cell-type-specific patterns and disease-associated remodeling. Integration with human genetics implicates suprabasal keratinocytes in atopic dermatitis and keratinocyte carcinomas, linked to higher and lower p16 and p21 expression, respectively. These findings establish GenVinci as a framework mapping senescence in 3D across scales.
